title: Fallback cohort tokenizer alignment sprint
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: as part of smart routing we route by region and tier and sometimes degrade to cheaper/nearby model variants. Observed risk: mismatches between primary and fallback variants (tokenization boundaries, context length trimming, and SDK/tooling flags) cause subtle hallucination and scoring regressions when requests fall back. Goal: run a focused sprint to maintain and extend the compatibility matrix for fallback cohorts so that tokenizer, context window semantics, and tooling flags are guaranteed or explicitly annotated for every variant pair used by routing policies. Scope: audit current matrix entries for region-tied variants, add automated checks in CI, produce remediation PRs for tokenizer configuration mismatches, and publish an ops playbook for resolving live fallbacks with minimal customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: All active fallback pairs used by region/tier routing are enumerated in the matrix
CI job added to verify tokenizer byte-level equivalence for each pair (or documents approved semantic delta)
Regression harness added to evaluate top-3 generation differences when failing to fallback variant across 3 representative prompt cohorts
Ops playbook published and linked in Console runbook for on-call to triage fallback-induced anomalies
Two high-risk mismatches (if found) remediated by updating tokenizer config or adding explicit routing exclusions
tasks: Inventory current fallback pairs referenced by routing policies (region & tier) — ENG-owned
Define byte-level tokenizer parity test and edge-case normalization rules
Add context-window and tool-flag validation to variant metadata schema
Implement CI job that runs tokenizer parity across sample corpora and emits a human-review ticket if non-deterministic
Run regression harness on canary traffic and capture tokenization mismatch examples
Open PRs to align tokenizers or add annotated divergence notes in model catalog
Draft and publish on-call remediation playbook (steps, dashboards, and rollback guidance)
comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha Patel: Kickoff — documented hypothesis that fallbacks in eu-west are causing higher rerank divergence; initial inventory started.
2026-02-18 Marco Gonzalez: Found 12 routing pairs where tokenizer normalization flags differed (strip_accents vs preserve). Prioritizing the 3 highest QPS pairs for immediate fixes.

2026-02-25 Engineering review: Decided to prefer conservative normalization (preserve) for fallbacks to avoid semantic token shifts; trade-off is slightly larger token counts and cost increase for those routes.
2026-03-02 QA: CI prototype added at ci/tokenizer-parity; it flags non-equal token sequences and emits sample prompts for review. False positives reduced by adding whitespace normalization step.
2026-03-05 PM review (Sofia Li): Agreed to annotate the catalog for remaining non-parity pairs rather than block rollout; catalog annotations will surface in Console routing UI.
2026-03-10 Ops note: Canary run on eu-west -> us-west fallback path shows 0.7% request-level semantic delta on scoring cohort; created follow-up ENG-131122 for deeper evaluation.
2026-03-12 Marco Gonzalez: Merged PRs to unify tokenizer config for pair cohort alpha/beta. Updating CI thresholds and publishing draft ops playbook.
2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Next steps — add telemetry alerts for sudden increase in token length variance and schedule cross-team demo with SDK and Console teams on 2026-03-18.
telemetry_checks: latency P95 change when switching to unified tokenizer config
rollout_plan: Stage 2: Canary fixes for top-3 pairs restricted to 5% traffic for 48h
Stage 3: If canary passes, expand to 25% for 24h and monitor rank-stability metrics
Stage 4: Full rollout and catalog annotation for any remaining non-parity pairs
Rollback: revert tokenizer config PR or add routing exclusion for affected pairs
